correctness.rationale: A pointed transitive action of the named commuting bijections is isomorphic to Z²/L with its zero coset, and the stabilizer does not depend on the point because the acting group is abelian. Isomorphism preserves the semantics even with tests, nesting and converse; vectors in the symmetric difference of two lattices yield distinguishing loops. The normal form (a,0),(b,c), ac=d, 0≤b<a counts exactly sigma_1(d) subgroups, and summing the triangular floor counts gives pi²*N²/12+O(N log N). For distinct lattices with an index d<N minimal, the lattice of index d has a generator of norm ≤d absent from the other lattice (containment with those index inequalities is impossible). At equal index N, both HNF generators are short when a,c≥2. Otherwise either (1,0), (b,1) for b≤N−2, or (1,−1) when b=N−1 is short and primitive, and a primitive vector determines at most one index-N lattice via the infinite cyclic quotient by that vector. The special parity lattice for N=2 lacks both unit vectors, but each other index-two lattice has one. The consecutive cycles N and N−1 with g trivial give exact lower length N−1. Without loop, simultaneous induction makes each program serial or empty and each formula constant across all these models: atomic actions and converses are serial, tests use constant formulas, and star is always serial. A separately coded BFS applying actual generators and inverses reproduced all 339 quotient actions through index 20, separation at every corresponding radius, and the exact consecutive-cycle witnesses.
residual_risks: Sharpness is for one uncompressed flat loop word, not arbitrary program expressions or formula size. The finite action calculation does not prove the statement for unbounded indices.
